answer: Each identity forges one marble token and must mirror it: each epoch the protocol pairs every identity with a peer, and both must co-sign each other's marble hash inside one 60-second falcon window. One operator behind k fake identities faces k independent windows colliding with probability 1-(59/60)^(k-1); each miss triggers a window-collision cascade slashing 2% of that identity's locked stake. Cost per fake identity: one dedicated signing device plus an expected 0.02*k*stake slash per epoch, so the k-th fake costs k times the first and total sybil cost grows quadratically in k.
